cards.title: Differentiate a saturated product with a new avatar instead of a new mechanism
cards.summary: When your product has no genuine mechanical or visual differentiation, compete by finding an unserved buyer group rather than fighting incumbents head-on.
cards.use_when: You are sourcing or marketing a saturated dropshipping product (e.g., an AB stimulator) and deciding how to enter a market dominated by 7-figure brands.
steps: Identify the problem your product solves and the mainstream avatar competitors already target.
Recognise that competing for the same avatar means fighting a bigger budget, better creative, better offers and higher tolerated CPA — the source says you may only get 'scraps'.

Assess whether you have a genuinely new mechanism: something visually, mechanically or functionally different that promises to solve the existing problem in a new way. The source argues most AliExpress dropshipping products do not offer this.
If you lack a new mechanism, pursue a new avatar: a group that wants the product's outcome but is not being marketed to, so there is little or no paid competition.
Prioritise differentiation above all else when choosing between candidate avatars; overwhelming evidence of an unserved group struggling with the problem is the source's stated selection criterion.
caveats: The source attributes much of the differentiation advantage to a new avatar, but a truly new product mechanism can also work — this is a situational alternative, not an absolute rule.
The '100K/month' framing is the source's own goal and case example, not a guaranteed outcome.

cards.title: Use Facebook Ad Library to map and exclude the mainstream avatar
cards.summary: Scan competitor creatives in the Ad Library to build a psychographic profile of the avatar you must avoid competing against.
cards.use_when: You need to know which demographics and desires incumbents already own before choosing an untapped avatar.
steps: Open Facebook Ad Library and search your product keyword (e.g., 'ab stimulator').
Identify the brands that appear to be scaling — repeated creatives, many variations, professional production.
Play video ads and note visible people: approximate age, gender and body type (the source estimated middle-aged men roughly early 40s to mid-60s).
Record what desires and USPs the creative appeals to (e.g., defined abs, hands-free use while working).
Note whether messaging assumes product awareness — speaking to people who know the category but need convincing why yours is better.
Repeat across as many successful competitors as you can until the mainstream avatar picture is stable.
caveats: Access to tools that estimate ad spend or traffic (such as third-party ad spy software) can speed this up; verify current functionality before relying on it.
Avatar inference from creatives is approximate — the source calls his own age read a 'spitball' estimate.

cards.title: Mine Amazon reviews for outlier buyer stories
cards.summary: Long Amazon reviews that narrate a buyer's life reveal alternative avatars distinct from the mainstream target.
cards.use_when: After mapping the incumbent avatar, you want candidate buyer segments your product already serves but competitors ignore.
steps: Go to the highest-review-count listing in your general category — it need not be the exact product.
Sort reviews by 'Top reviews'; filter to reviews containing images or videos, and consider scanning positive reviews for life-story detail.
Prioritise reviews where people describe their whole situation (weight history, surgery, stress, age, physical limitations) — these are the 'gold mines'.
Skip short generic reviews; they rarely reveal usable avatar information.
Record each distinct profile as a candidate avatar numbered in a document (e.g., 'Avatar 1: postpartum woman with C-section pooch').
Aim to leave the session with three to four different potential avatar ideas before deep-diving any one.
caveats: Store only the profile insight, not identifiable personal details from reviewers — the source explicitly flags this ethical concern.
Review visibility and sorting options on Amazon change over time; confirm the current interface.

cards.title: Validate avatar market size and problem severity on Reddit
cards.summary: Search Reddit threads to confirm a candidate avatar is a real, recurring, emotionally acute problem with enough people to scale against.
cards.use_when: You have a candidate avatar from review mining and need evidence it is large and painful enough to justify a campaign.
steps: Turn the review detail into a search query (e.g., 'post C-section weight gain Reddit') and review the resulting threads.
Check volume and recency of threads: many active discussions indicate a prominent, recurring problem rather than a one-off.
Read threads for how people describe the problem in their own words, how it makes them feel, their existing beliefs and their failed solutions.
Capture verbatim vocabulary (e.g., 'C-section pooch'), beliefs (e.g., 'surgery is the only way to get a flat stomach') and emotional states (self-image, body confidence).
Confirm the product's outcome directly addresses the pain — e.g., a stimulator promising a tighter midsection for a woman who desperately wants one.
caveats: The source requires a 'heavy burden of proof' that the avatar genuinely struggles with the problem and that enough such people exist before committing.
The source calls weight-loss fitness evergreen, but this is his assertion, not a guarantee for every niche.

cards.title: Assemble a raw avatar profile before deep research
cards.summary: Compile the observational evidence from ads and reviews into a bare-bones avatar sketch that deep research can later expand.
cards.use_when: You are between discovery and deep research and need a structured starting input for an AI prompt or manual research.
steps: Write a rough demographic band from Ad Library observations (e.g., men early 40s–mid-60s; or women late 20s–early 40s postpartum).
State the core problem in the avatar's own language (e.g., 'C-section pooch', flabbiness around the midsection).
List desires and valued USPs competitors emphasise (e.g., hands-free, use while working or cooking).
Record known beliefs and failed solutions (e.g., believes surgery is the only path; has tried cheap knockoff devices).
Mark this document as preliminary — the source stresses it is not yet a real avatar, only a general profile.
Repeat for each candidate avatar so you have several to test.
caveats: Do not mistake the preliminary sketch for a finished avatar record; the value comes from the subsequent deep research.

cards.title: Run an AI deep-research prompt to produce a full avatar report
cards.summary: Feed a preliminary avatar sketch to ChatGPT or Gemini in deep-research mode to synthesise psychology, beliefs and verbatim language from public sources into a long report.
cards.use_when: You have prioritised one avatar and need comprehensive psychological and situational detail before writing copy.
steps: Enable deep research in ChatGPT or Gemini (the source notes deep research alone was sufficient, search did not need to be separate).
Paste your prompt template and replace only the placeholder with the specific avatar — keep the rest identical for comparability.
Include the avatar name/identifier and the raw profile: demographics, problem, desires, known beliefs, failed solutions.

Instruct the model to cover: demographics and identity, avatar synopsis, day-to-day life struggles, how the problem makes them feel, how they describe it in their own words, prior failed solutions, limiting beliefs, existing beliefs about solutions (surgery, competing products), core identity beliefs, attitudes, hopes and dreams.
Wait for completion — the source's run took roughly 22 minutes and produced a 30+ page report.
Expect each claim to be backed by cited evidence and specific quotes from discussion forums, Reddit, social comments and other public sources.
Read the output manually, then click through to the cited sources line by line yourself.
caveats: The source found Gemini wider in depth of sources while ChatGPT was slightly less deep in his one comparison — this is a single-run observation, not a stable benchmark.
Do not paste outputs straight into ads; use them as research that you personally verify.

cards.title: Prioritise avatars with zero paid competition over better-known segments
cards.summary: Choose the avatar that appears completely isolated from existing advertising, provided the burden of proof on size and pain is met.
cards.use_when: You have two or three candidate avatars and must pick one to build a campaign around.
steps: Rank candidates primarily by differentiation: which group is currently unserved by Facebook advertisers.
A totally unmarketed avatar that wants your product's outcome is the source's stated 'gold mine' because there is no competition.
Before committing, verify three things: the avatar genuinely struggles with the problem, enough such people exist, and they desperately want what the product does.
Consider adjacent unserved pockets from the same reviews — e.g., seniors with pre-existing conditions who cannot easily get to a gym and still want abs.
If a group has overwhelming evidence and an obvious fit, that is the one to take into deep research first.
caveats: An isolated avatar can be commercially thin; the source pairs this with a heavy proof requirement for exactly that reason.
Do not choose solely on novelty if the avatar lacks urgency or buying desire.

cards.title: Turn the avatar record into copy-ready psychological inputs
cards.summary: A complete avatar record should contain the specific categories of insight that feed long-form ad copy and creative.
cards.use_when: You are finalising research to hand off to copywriting or creative development (the source routes writing to a separate copy module).
steps: Capture demographics and identity: who the person is and what defines them.
Document day-to-day life struggles and how the problem manifests in daily life.
Record how the problem makes them feel and the exact words they use to describe it.
List everything they have tried before and why it failed, if applicable.
Extract limiting beliefs (e.g., 'surgery is the only way to get a flat stomach') and existing beliefs about solutions in the category.
Note attitudes, hopes, dreams and beliefs that hold them back.
Use these categories directly as the raw material for advertising copy and creative angles.
caveats: Avatar work is deliberately separated from media buying, landing pages and product engineering — keep those decisions out of this record.

cards.title: Match the differentiation route to the product's actual state
cards.summary: If you have a genuinely different product, compete on a new mechanism; if it is the same commodity item, compete on a new avatar.
cards.use_when: Deciding strategy at the start of marketing a product in a saturated or dropshipped category.
steps: Audit the product for real differentiation: is it visually, mechanically or functionally unique versus the standard listing?
If yes, build a new mechanism narrative — a new cause of the problem and a new promised solution the audience has not heard.
If no, accept that a new mechanism is not credible (the source argues most AliExpress products lack this) and pursue a new avatar instead.
Recognise that a new mechanism often performs best when you are actually creating something new, not reskinning an existing item with a fresh claim.
Choose the route first, because avatar discovery, creative and offer all flow from it.
caveats: The source's preference for avatar over mechanism is opinion tied to commodity dropshipping, not a universal law.
Claiming a new mechanism without real product difference risks the audience disbelieving you.

input.text:
02-AVT / avatars and jobs to be done

Goes here. Discovering untapped customer avatars to bypass market saturation for existing e-commerce products. Using competitive research to exclude already-targeted demographics, mining Amazon reviews for alternative buyer profiles, validating market size via Reddit, and using AI deep-research prompts to generate comprehensive psychological and situational records.

Not here.

Writing the ad creative, video scripts, or hooks based on the research -> 10-MCR

Media buying tactics, cost caps, and adset account structures -> 11-ADC

Designing pre-landers or product pages to convert the new avatar -> 07-LPG

Engineering a new mechanical feature or physical product differentiation -> 01-PRD

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: A specific four-step pipeline (competitive exclusion, Amazon review mining, Reddit validation, and AI deep-research) to uncover and define profitable, untapped e-commerce avatars for saturated products. modules: [AVT] topics: [research method, review mining, segmentation, avatar record structure] tier: 4 scope_hint: mixed

Topics. research method / utilizing Facebook Ad Library for competitor exclusion, mining Amazon reviews for outlier buyer stories, confirming market size via Reddit forums, and deploying ChatGPT/Gemini deep-research prompts. segmentation / pivoting saturated dropshipping products to unserved sub-markets (e.g., marketing an AB stimulator to postpartum women or 65+ seniors instead of middle-aged men) to avoid competing on CPA against 7-figure brands. avatar record structure / compiling demographics, daily life struggles, emotional mind states, verbatim vocabulary, failed past solutions, and limiting beliefs.

Look for. The 4-step discovery framework: 1) Competitive research in Facebook Ad Library to identify and exclude the current mainstream avatar; 2) Review mining on Amazon (sorting by "Top reviews" or "Images/Videos") to find long, detailed life stories from alternative users; 3) Ideating on Reddit (e.g., searching "post C-section weight gain Reddit") to confirm market viability and problem severity; 4) Deep research using AI prompts to synthesize a 30+ page report on the avatar's psychology. Specific avatar record requirements: demographics, day-to-day life struggles, feelings about the problem, verbatim descriptions, failed solutions, and limiting beliefs (e.g., "surgery is the only way to get a flat stomach").

Skip. Revenue bragging, generic dropshipping motivational content, or student shoutouts (e.g., "hitting 100K a month"). Tactical media buying advice (e.g., cost caps, number of adsets), which is explicitly excluded by the source and belongs in 11-ADC.

Scope mix. The core need to define an avatar's struggle and job is baseline. The specific AI deep-research prompt workflow and competitive exclusion tactics to pivot saturated products are growth.

Volume. 25 to 35.
